opener.label: Part I
opener.title: See
opener.subtitle: A perceptron recognises a digit
opener.posterLabel: Your drawing as the network receives it: 784 dots on a 28 x 28 grid, the area of each dot shows how much ink there is

pad.label: Drawing area
pad.hint: Enter: pen down or up. Arrows: move.

ch1.body: A network of {count} parameters recognises it live, in your browser.<sup>1</sup> Nothing is sent to a server.
ch1.note: The ten stems are the output probabilities, one per digit; they add up to 1.
ch1.noteAlmost: Here, the {digit} takes nearly all of it.
ch1.caption: The drawing, the prediction and the ten output probabilities.
ch1.captionLive: The drawing, the prediction and the ten output probabilities: the {digit} wins with {percent}.
ch1.probsLabel: Output probabilities: the {digit} at {percent}, the nine other digits share the rest

status.error: The network could not be loaded. Reload the page to try again.
status.empty: Draw a digit to start the prediction.

ch2.body: Your drawing is cropped and fitted into a 20 x 20 square, centred,<sup>2</sup> then turned into 784 numbers between 0 and 1: that is all the network receives.<sup>3</sup>
ch2.note2: The 20 x 20 frame leaves a margin of 4 pixels on each side, like the MNIST images.
ch2.note3: A 7 with a crossbar, the European way? This network was trained on American handwriting (MNIST) and reads it as a 3, at {percent}.
ch2.gridLabel: The 28 x 28 pixel image sent to the network, with the 20 x 20 frame that holds the drawing.
ch2.gridHint: Hover over it or use the arrow keys to move the magnifier.
ch2.detailLabel: Enlarged detail of 6 x 6 pixels with their values, from 0 for the background to 1 for full ink
ch2.caption: The image sent to the network: 28 x 28 dots whose area shows the ink, the 20 x 20 frame in dotted outline and, enlarged, a detail of the drawing with its values. Move the magnifier over the image to read other pixels.

ch3.body: Each layer recombines the output of the previous one.<sup>4</sup> Out of 256 neurons, {first} light up in the first hidden layer and {second} in the second; the others stay at zero.

input.title: Input
input.label: Input: the 784 pixels of the image

hidden1.title: Hidden layer 1
hidden1.labelBest: Hidden layer 1: activations of the 256 neurons, neuron {neuron} is the most active
hidden1.labelPicked: Hidden layer 1: activations of the 256 neurons, neuron {neuron} is selected
hidden1.pick: Hidden layer 1, neuron picker. Use the arrow keys to select a neuron.

hidden2.title: Hidden layer 2
hidden2.label: Hidden layer 2: activations of the 256 neurons

output.title: Output
output.label: Output: the neuron for {digit} is the brightest of the ten
output.labelSure: Output: the neuron for {digit} is lit, the other nine are off

ch3.caption: The network, layer after layer: each dot is a neuron and its area is its activation. Neuron {neuron}, in orange, is the most active in the first layer. Click a dot in the first layer to inspect it.
ch3.captionPicked: The network, layer after layer: each dot is a neuron and its area is its activation. Neuron {neuron}, in orange, is the one you are inspecting. Click a dot in the first layer to change it.

ch4.body: A neuron in the first layer assigns a weight to each of the 784 pixels.<sup>5</sup> Redrawn as 28 x 28, these weights show the shape that excites it and the one that silences it.
ch4.note: Nobody drew these weights: they tuned themselves during training, example after example.
ch4.title: Neuron {neuron} of layer 1
ch4.fieldLabel: Weights of neuron {neuron}: 784 values mapped back onto the 28 x 28 grid, solid dots are excitatory, rings are inhibitory
ch4.seeksText: Its 784 weights mapped back onto the image grid: the ink it expects on one side, the ink that holds it back on the other.

status.error: The weights could not be loaded.

ch4.scaleLabel: Weight scale, from -1 to 1: a ring for a negative weight, a solid dot for a positive weight, the area grows with the absolute value

activation.label: Activation
activation.best: the most active in the layer, normalised value
activation.some: normalised value, 1 being the most active in the layer
activation.off: off for this drawing, set to zero by the ReLU

ch4.caption: The 784 weights of neuron {neuron} mapped back onto the image grid: solid dots excitatory, rings inhibitory, area proportional to the weight.
